_comment: Audio quality thresholds (SRS Step 13, FR xii-xiv, xxxvii). Each check gives a grade; the recording's grade is the worst one. Levels are dBFS (0 = digital full scale). Used for dataset clips, uploads and live windows.
_duration: Shorter than 0.3 s is Unusable (nothing to classify); longer than 10 minutes is Poor for an upload.
_silence: Peak below -60 dBFS is Unusable. If more than 95 % of frames are below -60 dBFS the recording is Poor (mostly silent).
_level: Level of the active (non-silent) part. Below about -48 dBFS little headroom is left above typical microphone self-noise; below -55 dBFS detail is lost even after normalization. (MIMII records at about -45 dBFS, which is quiet but clean on 16-bit audio.)
_clipping: A sample counts as clipped when it sits at >= 0.99 of full scale for 3+ consecutive samples (one peak touching full scale is not clipping).

noise._note: Noise-dominated = the level barely changes over time (small gap between loud and quiet frames) AND the spectrum is noise-like (high flatness). Both are required, so a steady siren or hum (tonal, low flatness) is not called noisy. Skipped for the Background Noise class, which is noise by definition.

_dropouts: Runs of exact digital zeros of 20 ms or more in the middle of the recording are missing frames. Leading/trailing zeros are padding, not dropouts.
_sample_rate: Below 16 kHz the recording lacks part of the 0-8 kHz band the models use.
